exposure: intrapartum cesarean delivery for both twins
intrapartum cesarean delivery for the second twin (combined delivery)
outcome: intrapartum cesarean delivery for one or both twins
Apgar score lower than 7 at 5 minutes
cohort: The study included 69,172 participants with twin gestations who attempted vaginal delivery after 35 weeks of gestation, using natality data from the United States.
finding: Intrapartum cesarean delivery in twin gestations was found to be more prevalent than previously reported and was associated with adverse perinatal outcomes, with previous cesarean delivery and nulliparity being strong associated factors.
mod_finding: Intrapartum cesarean delivery, whether for both twins or combined delivery, was associated with higher risks of maternal transfusion, maternal intensive care unit admission, and lower Apgar scores at 5 minutes compared with successful vaginal delivery of both twins.
